subject.title: fix(telegram): Allow multi-agent ACP bindings within same account

question: Should same-account Telegram ACP binds in one group topic be an explicit single-owner handoff, or should OpenClaw support multiple simultaneous addressable bindings for that same account/topic?
rationale: The current manager and session-binding service expose one resolved binding per account/topic; true simultaneous bindings need a broader routing and storage design than the PR's conflict-filter change.

options.title: Rework As Single-Owner Handoff
options.body: Preserve the current one-binding-per-topic model, allow same-account replacement deliberately, and update tests/proof to describe ownership handoff rather than independent bindings.

options.title: Design True Multi-Binding Semantics
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define how inbound messages choose among multiple same-topic ACP sessions and how those bindings are stored, resolved, touched, and unbound.

options.title: Keep Current Fence
options.body: Reject the same-account exception for now and keep the cross-owner fence unchanged until a narrower user report proves the desired behavior.

recommendation.title: Rework As Single-Owner Handoff
recommendation.body: Preserve the current one-binding-per-topic model, allow same-account replacement deliberately, and update tests/proof to describe ownership handoff rather than independent bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recently owned the Telegram thread-binding storage and migration boundary that determines the safe implementation shape.
